Summary of essential results:

- Study compares a gas absorption heat pump (GAHP) and a electric air-source heat pump (ASHP) for space heating (and cooling) of a small office building across nine Canadian cities.
- GAHP’s seasonal performance (SCOP) is lower than the electric ASHP in all nine cities.
- Despite lower SCOP, GAHP often offers lower annual fuel costs:
  - GAHP has 13%–83% lower annual fuel costs than electric ASHP during heating in the nine cities.
  - When cooling is included, GAHP is cost-effective in seven of the nine cities, though fuel cost savings are smaller.
- Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions:
  - GAHP emits fewer GHGs than the electric ASHP in two of the nine cities; in other cities emissions are comparable or higher depending on grid electricity emissions.
- Key finding: GAHP is more advantageous for heating (and cooling) in cities with:
  - Lower natural gas prices relative to electricity prices.
  - Higher emission intensity of the electrical grid.
- Practical tool: A screening method is developed to extend results to other cities using only heating/cooling degree days and the electricity-to-gas price ratio, aiding designers and owners in choosing between GAHP and electric ASHP for their location.
results.title: A method for climate-based comparison of gas absorption and electric air-source heat pumps based on fuel costs and emissions

Summary:
- Topic and method: The study analyzes how backup fuel choices in cold-climate residential heating affect environmental, economic, and grid outcomes when using heat pumps. It uses an hourly techno-economic model for 6,000 nationally representative Canadian homes, comparing heat pumps with electric backup, natural gas backup, and new conventional furnaces.
- Key findings:
  - Electrifying heating with heat pumps (with full electric backup) can reduce annual space heating and cooling energy use by over 59% and cut national residential GHG emissions by up to 21 million tonnes CO2e per year compared with new conventional furnaces.
  - However, without supportive policy, only about 9% of households save money with fully electric heating systems, and such electrification can raise peak electricity demand.
  - Hybrid systems with gas backup (hybrid gas-backup) have smaller impacts on peak electricity demand and greenhouse gas reductions than fully electric systems.
- Implications: Decarbonization via heat pumps is technically beneficial for emissions and energy use but requires policy or market measures to ensure homeowner cost savings and to manage potential increases in peak electricity load. Hybrid backup options offer a compromise with less strain on the grid but also somewhat reduced emissions reductions.
results.title: The role of backup fuel in residential electrification: assessing the environmental, economic, and grid impacts of heat pump backup systems in cold-climate residential

results.search_result:
- Cold climate heat pumps can work in real winters, but running cost depends on fuel you compare against.
- Against natural gas in cold states: most heat pumps do not beat gas on cost. You need a COP between 3.4 and 5.4 to break even, which no unit maintains through a northern winter.
- Against oil or propane: heat pumps usually win on cost. A COP of about 1.1 to 2.8 is sufficient for most of the heating season, and good cold-climate units typically achieve this into the teens Fahrenheit.
- Real-world performance (two federal field studies):
  - PNNL: median COP of 1.9 in the 0–5°F band (22 units).
  - NREL: in some cases, resistance heat consumed more energy than the compressor; performance varies with install quality.
- Key conditions for favorable economics:
  - Proper sizing and commissioning (avoid oversizing; ensure good load calculations).
  - Minimize reliance on auxiliary resistance heat (lowers efficiency/higher cost).
  - Consider dual-fuel setups (gas furnace plus heat pump) for cold extremes, with a proper crossover setting.
- Practical steps for evaluating costs:
  1) Use your actual electricity and fuel bills (state averages are less reliable than your bill).
  2) Check unit COP at 47°F, 17°F, and 5°F to compare with your fuel’s cost targets.
  3) If using gas, consider dual-fuel operation to maximize savings.
  4) Ensure proper load calculation to avoid oversizing and increased backup heat.
  5) Verify auxiliary heat lockout settings to limit costly resistance heat.
results.title: Cold Climate Heat Pump Running Cost, by State

- Between Feb 2 and Sep 1, 2026, residential gas prices (incl. taxes) rose about 12% across EU capital cities; electricity prices rose about 4.2%.
- Early Sep 2026 residential electricity prices (incl. taxes) ranged from 8.4 c€/kWh (Kyiv) to 41.3 c€/kWh (Brussels); EU average across capitals: 27.2 c€/kWh. Highest by city: Berlin, Dublin, Bern, London; mid-range: Rome, Vienna, Prague; lowest: Budapest, Podgorica, Belgrade, Valletta.
- Gas prices (incl. taxes) ranged from 1.5 c€/kWh (Kyiv) to 34.8 c€/kWh (Stockholm); EU average across capitals: 11.9 c€/kWh. Among large economies, Paris most expensive for gas (15.7 c€/kWh); Madrid (10.1 c€/kWh) and London (10.3 c€/kWh) cheapest among them.
- Within cities, electricity rose most in Lisbon (+22%), Amsterdam (+17.3%), Madrid (+15.1%), Rome (+14.9%); largest declines: Luxembourg City (-15.3%), Tallinn (-7.9%), Helsinki (-7.1%).
- Energy bills are potentially higher due to lower gas storage levels (EU storage ~72.4% full on Oct 3), leaving Europe more exposed to cold spells and relying on tariff structures and government support to dampen bills.

Summary:

- Purpose: The Winter Heating Costs by State, 2026–27 report combines EIA data on main heating fuel shares, state fuel prices, and typical winter usage to estimate a household heating bill from November through March for every state and DC.

- Core findings:
  - Natural gas is the most common heating fuel (about 51% of homes), electricity is second (about 34%). Propane and heating oil/kerosene are minor nationally (each ~4%), but are significant in some states.

## Heat Pumps vs. Gas Furnaces in Cold Climates: A Cost Analysis

This report summarizes the cost-effectiveness of heat pumps versus gas furnaces in cold climates, based on recent research.

### **Cost Comparison**

*   **Heat Pumps vs. Natural Gas:**
    *   In cold climates, most heat pumps typically do not offer lower running costs than natural gas furnaces [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   A coefficient of performance (COP) between 3.4 and 5.4 is generally needed for a heat pump to break even with natural gas on cost during a northern winter, a level that most units do not sustain [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   A study comparing gas absorption heat pumps (GAHP) and electric air-source heat pumps (ASHP) across nine Canadian cities found that GAHP often results in 13%–83% lower annual fuel costs for heating than electric ASHPs [harvest.usask.ca](https://harvest.usask.ca/items/135e690b-94bb-43f0-b469-8f42bd69166d/full). Even when cooling is included, GAHP is more cost-effective in seven of the nine cities [harvest.usask.ca](https://harvest.usask.ca/items/135e690b-94bb-43f0-b469-8f42bd69166d/full).
    *   A GAHP is more advantageous for heating and cooling in areas with lower natural gas prices relative to electricity prices [harvest.usask.ca](https://harvest.usask.ca/items/135e690b-94bb-43f0-b469-8f42bd69166d/full).
    *   Projections for winter 2026-2027 in the US estimate an average per-home spending of $640 for natural gas and $1,196 for electricity used for heating [centdaily.com](https://centdaily.com/reports/winter-heating-cost-report-2026). Overall, electricity is typically 1.6 times the cost of natural gas for winter uses [centdaily.com](https://centdaily.com/reports/winter-heating-cost-report-2026).
    *   In the US, gas heating bills are projected to range from $278 to $1,401, while electricity heating bills are projected to range from $695 to $1,925 [centdaily.com](https://centdaily.com/reports/winter-heating-cost-report-2026).

*   **Heat Pumps vs. Oil or Propane:**
    *   Heat pumps generally offer lower running costs than oil or propane heating systems [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   A COP of approximately 1.1 to 2.8 is sufficient for a heat pump to be cost-effective against oil or propane for most of the heating season [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/). Good cold-climate heat pump units typically maintain this COP into the teens Fahrenheit [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   Projections for winter 2026-2027 in the US estimate an average per-home spending of $2,115 for heating oil and $1,246 for propane [centdaily.com](https://centdaily.com/reports/winter-heating-cost-report-2026). Heating oil costs are about 3.4 times the cost of natural gas, and propane bills typically range from $1,031 to $2,036 [centdaily.com](https://centdaily.com/reports/winter-heating-cost-report-2026).

### **Factors Influencing Cost-Effectiveness**

*   **Fuel Prices:**
    *   Natural gas and electricity prices are key determinants of heating costs [harvest.usask.ca](https://harvest.usask.ca/items/135e690b-94bb-43f0-b469-8f42bd69166d/full).
    *   In Europe, residential gas prices increased by about 12% and electricity prices by about 4.2% across EU capital cities between February and September 2026 [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/winter-energy-bills-where-are-gas-and-electricity-prices-highest-in-europe).
    *   The average residential electricity price in EU capitals in early September 2026 was 27.2 c€/kWh, ranging from 8.4 c€/kWh to 41.3 c€/kWh [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/winter-energy-bills-where-are-gas-and-electricity-prices-highest-in-europe). The average residential gas price was 11.9 c€/kWh, ranging from 1.5 c€/kWh to 34.8 c€/kWh [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/winter-energy-bills-where-are-gas-and-electricity-prices-highest-in-europe).
    *   New York State residential natural gas prices in 2026 ranged from $16.01/MCF in January to $30.86/MCF in July [nyserda.ny.gov](https://www.nyserda.ny.gov/Energy-Prices/Natural-Gas/Monthly-Average-Price-of-Natural-Gas-Residential).

*   **System Performance and Installation:**
    *   Proper sizing and commissioning are crucial for favorable heat pump economics, including avoiding oversizing and ensuring accurate load calculations [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   Minimizing reliance on auxiliary resistance heat, which is less efficient and more costly, is important [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   Real-world performance studies show median COPs of 1.9 for heat pumps in the 0–5°F band, but performance varies with installation quality [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).

*   **Hybrid Systems:**
    *   Dual-fuel setups combining a gas furnace with a heat pump can maximize savings, especially in extreme cold, by using a proper crossover setting [heatpumpmath.com](https://heatpumpmath.com/cold-climate-heat-pump-cost/).
    *   Hybrid systems with gas backup for heat pumps have a smaller impact on peak electricity demand compared to fully electric systems [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).

### **Environmental and Grid Impacts**

*   **Emissions:**
    *   Electrifying heating with heat pumps (with full electric backup) can reduce annual space heating and cooling energy use by over 59% and cut national residential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by up to 21 million tonnes CO2e per year compared to conventional furnaces [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).
    *   Gas absorption heat pumps emit fewer GHGs than electric air-source heat pumps in some cities, with emissions comparable or higher in others depending on the emission intensity of the electrical grid [harvest.usask.ca](https://harvest.usask.ca/items/135e690b-94bb-43f0-b469-8f42bd69166d/full).

*   **Grid Impact:**
    *   Fully electric heating systems can increase peak electricity demand [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).
    *   Hybrid systems with gas backup have less strain on the grid [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).

### **Policy and Market Considerations**

*   Decarbonization through heat pumps is technically beneficial for emissions and energy use, but policies or market measures are needed to ensure cost savings for homeowners and to manage potential increases in peak electricity load [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).
*   Without supportive policy, only about 9% of households save money with fully electric heating systems [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.116963).

sources.summary:
- Cold climate heat pumps can work in real winters, but running cost depends on fuel you compare against.
- Against natural gas in cold states: most heat pumps do not beat gas on cost. You need a COP between 3.4 and 5.4 to break even, which no unit maintains through a northern winter.
- Against oil or propane: heat pumps usually win on cost. A COP of about 1.1 to 2.8 is sufficient for most of the heating season, and good cold-climate units typically achieve this into the teens Fahrenheit.
- Real-world performance (two federal field studies):
  - PNNL: median COP of 1.9 in the 0–5°F band (22 units).
  - NREL: in some cases, resistance heat consumed more energy than the compressor; performance varies with install quality.
- Key conditions for favorable economics:
  - Proper sizing and commissioning (avoid oversizing; ensure good load calculations).
  - Minimize reliance on auxiliary resistance heat (lowers efficiency/higher cost).
  - Consider dual-fuel setups (gas furnace plus heat pump) for cold extremes, with a proper crossover setting.
- Practical steps for evaluating costs:
  1) Use your actual electricity and fuel bills (state averages are less reliable than your bill).
  2) Check unit COP at 47°F, 17°F, and 5°F to compare with your fuel’s cost targets.
  3) If using gas, consider dual-fuel operation to maximize savings.
  4) Ensure proper load calculation to avoid oversizing and increased backup heat.
  5) Verify auxiliary heat lockout settings to limit costly resistance heat.

results.query: LFP vs NMC battery performance metrics electric vehicles range charging cycles safety
results.search_result:
Summary:
- Study compares LFP and NMC lithium-ion batteries under realistic EV cycling across 25–65°C to diagnose and forecast State of Health (SOH).
- Both chemistries show faster degradation with rising temperature, but NMC ages much more rapidly above 50°C.
- Key SOH indicators (capacity fade, internal resistance growth, coulombic efficiency) worsen with temperature; NMC exhibits significantly higher degradation and greater variability under thermal stress.
- At 60°C, LFP retains ~80% SOH for roughly twice as many cycles as NMC; LFP also shows lower resistance growth and steadier coulombic efficiency across temperatures.
- Conclusion: LFP offers superior thermal resilience and longer cycle life under hot conditions; NMC is more vulnerable to thermal stress, especially above 50°C, impacting end-of-life timing and safety margins.
- Implication: Chemistry choice and thermal management are critical for EV deployments in hot climates or high-duty applications; results provide a multi-temperature simulation benchmark to aid adaptive battery management system design.
results.title: Comparative SOH Diagnosis and Forecasting of LFP and NMC Lithium-Ion Batteries in Electric Vehicles under Realistic Operating Conditions

results.query: LFP vs NMC battery performance metrics electric vehicles range charging cycles safety
results.search_result:
Here are the essential results from the study “Heat Generation and Fast Charging Characteristics of Automotive LFP, NMC, and NCA Battery Cells” by Thornton and Kollmeyer:

- Study scope: Experimental testing and modeling of four production fast-charging Li-ion cells (NMC, NCA, LFP) used in vehicles (Rivian R1S/T, BYD Dolphin, Porsche Taycan, Tesla Model 3/Y) with charging to 80% SOC in ~20 minutes.
- Heat generation: Entropic heating coefficients measured for each cell; combined with other data to quantify total heat generation during fast charging.
- Charge efficiency and losses: At a 3C charge rate, overall charge efficiency is about 90%, with substantial losses of roughly 18–24 kW when scaled to a 60 kWh pack.
- LFP-specific finding: LFP cells can charge to 100% SOC in less than half the time of the other chemistries, indicating a unique advantage in fast charging duration.
- Calorimetry vs. modeling: Calorimeter measurements of heat losses align reasonably well with models, with a discrepancy of only 5–17%—noting typical calorimeter inaccuracies.
- Overall takeaway: Despite substantial variation in energy density across chemistries, fast charging and heat generation characteristics are relatively similar, suggesting convergence in design goals among manufacturers to manage heat effectively during high-rate charging.
- Practical implication: Thermal management remains critical for maintaining fast charging performance; efficient management can enable similar high-rate charging across LFP, NMC, and NCA cells, with LFP offering an advantage in achieving full SOC more rapidly.
results.title: Heat Generation and Fast Charging Characteristics of Automotive LFP, NMC, and NCA Battery Cells by Jack Thornton, Phillip  J. Kollmeyer :: SSRN

results.query: LFP vs NMC battery performance metrics electric vehicles range charging cycles safety
results.search_result:
Summary:
- The study compares NMC and LFP lithium-ion chemistries in multiple cell formats (cylindrical and prismatic) and formats/speeds, evaluating charging/discharging performance, energy retention, power delivery, voltage patterns, and external heat.
- Key findings:
  - NMC cells deliver higher power output but generate more heat during fast charging; charging faster increases internal heat.
  - LFP cells run cooler with more consistent temperatures and lower surface temperatures, though typically with different energy delivery characteristics.
  - Heat generation increases with higher charge currents (0.5C to 2C), shortening charge time but raising thermal load; thermal management becomes more critical at higher C-rates.
  - The effect of cell chemistry and structure on heat behavior, charge/discharge time, energy stored/recovered, and voltage patterns is significant; no single chemistry/format meets all performance criteria.
  - For EV applications:
    - Long-range cars: NMC may be preferable for higher energy delivery and range.
    - Buses, delivery vehicles, and stationary storage: LFP offers longer cycle life and lower heat risk, with more stable temperatures.
- Practical implication: Vehicle design and operation should tailor chemistry, cell format, and thermal management to duty patterns, charging routines, and budget; broader-scale testing beyond short lab tests is recommended to capture real-world degradation and thermal dynamics.
results.title: Comparative Analysis of Lithium-Ion Battery Chemistries and Cell Formats: Implications for Charging Performance, Discharge Behavior and Thermal Characteristics in Electric Vehicle Applications | IntechOpen

results.query: LFP vs NMC battery performance metrics electric vehicles range charging cycles safety
results.search_result:
Summary:
- The review maps how cell form factors (cylindrical, prismatic, pouch) and electrode architectures (jelly-roll, stacked, blade) affect performance, safety, and manufacturability across common LIB chemistries: LFP, NMC, NCA, and LCO.
- Key trade-offs:
  - LFP: lower voltage and energy density but superior thermal stability and cycle life; supports prismatic and blade formats well, aiding secure, cost-efficient integration in EVs and storage.
  - NMC/NCA: higher specific energy and power with jelly-roll architectures that benefit from tabless or multi-tab current collection for uniform current distribution and easier manufacturability; favored in cylindrical and pouch formats for high-energy applications.
  - LCO: highest energy density but limited by safety, cobalt cost, and shorter cycle life; mainly confined to small electronics.
- Form factor insights:
  - Cylindrical cells offer mechanical robustness and mature automation but lower volumetric energy density due to packing efficiency.
  - Prismatic and blade designs enable tighter packaging and higher energy density per volume, especially for LFP.
  - Pouch cells provide high energy-to-weight and flexible packaging but require precise mechanical compression for performance and safety.
- Electrode architecture insights:
  - Jelly-roll and multi-tab/tabless configurations improve uniform current distribution and enable higher energy/power in NMC/NCA chemistries.
  - Blade and stacked architectures influence manufacturability and thermal management, aligning with specific form factors.
- Underexplored area: LiMnFePO4 (LMFP) cathodes offer potential voltage and energy gains while maintaining cycle life and cost, but integration across forms and architectures needs more research.
- Practical takeaway: An application-driven framework is established to select optimal combinations of form factor and electrode design tailored to chemistry, performance targets, safety, and production capabilities, guiding next-generation LIB system design.
results.title: Comparative Analysis of Cell Design: Form Factor and Electrode Architectures in Advanced Lithium-Ion Batteries

results.query: LFP NMC battery cost comparison manufacturing process supply chain electric vehicles
results.search_result:
Summary:
- The main value in a lithium-ion cell is the cathode active material (CAM), which accounts for roughly 40–50% of a nickel-based cell’s cost and 25–30% of an LFP cell’s cost; cathode material is the most expensive and hardest-to-secure component.
- Britain has no commercial-scale cathode or anode material production (or separators) today; existing activity is at pilot/demonstration scale, with two working cell plants in Sunderland and a planned one in Somerset.
- Globally, CAM production is concentrated in China and many CAM producers have been operating at a loss since 2023, making private financing for new CAM plants difficult.
- Britain’s demand would only require about half a world-scale CAM plant; with Agratas at full size, it could support one or two plants.
- Trade rules by 2027 can be met with CAM imports from the EU or Britain, but British electricity costs are higher than the EU median for large users.
- Conclusion: No component currently is clearly economical to manufacture in Britain under today’s conditions. The most plausible domestic openings are separators and specialist anode materials; cathode material remains the highest value and hardest to establish.
- Strategic case for a British cathode industry exists but requires: a long-term CAM supply contract, electricity prices near European levels, substantial public capital or production support, and a foreign partner with process know-how. Without any one, a plant risks failure.
- Favored near-term policy/industry actions: back separators and specialist anode materials first (lighter capital and quicker wins), avoid public money for conventional electrolyte capacity in an oversupplied European market, and view cross-channel collaboration (e.g., a Polish cathode plant for Sunderland or a British separator plant for Germany) as strengthening the European supply chain.
- Additional note: Recycling/refining of recycled material could be a future route, as Europe expects to be short of that capacity, though Britain’s activity is currently at demonstration scale.
results.title: Battery Components Beyond the Gigafactory | ReindustrialiseUK

Summary:
- Q3 2026 saw broad price declines across most battery cell grades, with the pace and patterns differing by format and region.

## LFP vs. NMC Lithium-Ion Batteries for Electric Vehicles

This report compares Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) and Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) lithium-ion batteries, focusing on their characteristics and implications for electric vehicles (EVs).

### Performance and Durability

*   **Thermal Resilience and Degradation**
    *   LFP batteries offer superior thermal resilience and a longer cycle life under hot conditions [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489).
    *   NMC batteries degrade more rapidly than LFP batteries above 50°C and are more vulnerable to thermal stress [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489).
    *   At 60°C, LFP batteries retain approximately 80% State of Health (SOH) for roughly twice as many cycles as NMC batteries [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489).
    *   LFP batteries also show lower resistance growth and steadier coulombic efficiency across various temperatures compared to NMC [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489).
    *   NMC cells generate more heat during fast charging, while LFP cells run cooler with more consistent and lower surface temperatures [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182).

*   **Power and Energy Delivery**
    *   NMC cells generally deliver higher power output and are preferable for long-range cars due to higher energy delivery and range [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   LFP batteries typically have lower voltage and energy density compared to NMC [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   The use phase of NMC batteries generally outperforms LFP in energy efficiency due to lower battery mass [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.7302/27571).

*   **Fast Charging**
    *   LFP cells can charge to 100% SOH in less than half the time of other chemistries, offering a unique advantage in fast charging duration [papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7466288).
    *   Despite variations in energy density, fast charging and heat generation characteristics are relatively similar across LFP, NMC, and NCA cells, suggesting convergence in design goals among manufacturers to manage heat effectively [papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7466288).
    *   Thermal management is critical for maintaining fast charging performance, regardless of chemistry [papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7466288) [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182).

*   **Cycle Life**
    *   LFP batteries offer a longer cycle life [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450) [iea.org](https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-can-innovation-help-secure-future-battery-markets-and-mineral-supplies).
    *   NMC batteries generally have a shorter cycle life compared to LFP [reneweconomy.com.au](https://reneweconomy.com.au/batteries-and-cells-whether-on-wheels-or-the-grid-its-all-about-chemistry-and-cost/).

### Cost and Market Dynamics

*   **Cost of Materials and Cells**
    *   LFP chemistry replaces expensive nickel and cobalt, making LFP batteries generally cheaper than nickel-based cells [ljyenergy.com](https://ljyenergy.com/why-are-chinese-lithium-batteries-so-cheap/).
    *   The cathode active material (CAM) accounts for 40-50% of a nickel-based cell's cost and 25-30% of an LFP cell's cost, making it the most expensive and difficult-to-secure component [reindustrialiseuk.org](https://reindustrialiseuk.org/knowledgebase/battery-components-beyond-the-gigafactory/).
    *   In Q3 2026, LFP 314Ah prices fluctuated, rising in July and falling in August, but Europe and North America prices remained above China [source.benchmarkminerals.com](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/lithium-cost-pass-through-drives-volatile-quarter-for-energy-storage-cells-cell-price-review-q3-2026).
    *   LFP pack prices can be discounted by roughly 36.7% to over 40% compared to NMC [nextmsc.com](https://www.nextmsc.com/industry-deep-dive/lfp-vs-nmc-battery-share-by-region-2026).
    *   Lithium-ion battery prices have dropped over 90% from 2010–2024 [iea.org](https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-can-innovation-help-secure-future-battery-markets-and-mineral-supplies).

*   **Market Share and Production**
    *   LFP accounts for over 55% of deployed EV batteries worldwide [nextmsc.com](https://www.nextmsc.com/industry-deep-dive/lfp-vs-nmc-battery-share-by-region-2026).
    *   Outside China, about 80% of deployed EV batteries use nickel-containing chemistries (NMC) [nextmsc.com](https://www.nextmsc.com/industry-deep-dive/lfp-vs-nmc-battery-share-by-region-2026).
    *   China produces over 75% of global lithium-ion cells, with most supply chain components concentrated domestically, contributing to lower prices [ljyenergy.com](https://ljyenergy.com/why-are-chinese-lithium-batteries-so-cheap/) [mckinsey.com.br](https://www.mckinsey.com.br/features/mckinsey-center-for-future-mobility/our-insights/battery-2035-building-new-advantages).
    *   The current EV battery mix is roughly 50/50 between LFP and NMC, with LFP being the fastest-growing due to lower cost and longer cycle life [iea.org](https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-can-innovation-help-secure-future-battery-markets-and-mineral-supplies).
    *   Chinese producers supply about 75% of global EV battery deployment [nextmsc.com](https://www.nextmsc.com/industry-deep-dive/lfp-vs-nmc-battery-share-by-region-2026).

*   **Overcapacity and Pricing Trends**
    *   Overcapacity in the battery market (about 900 GWh in 2025) persists, mainly driven by Asian manufacturers [mckinsey.com.br](https://www.mckinsey.com.br/features/mckinsey-center-for-future-mobility/our-insights/battery-2035-building-new-advantages).
    *   Q3 2026 saw broad price declines across most battery cell grades [source.benchmarkminerals.com](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/lithium-cost-pass-through-drives-volatile-quarter-for-energy-storage-cells-cell-price-review-q3-2026).
    *   The global Lithium Ion Battery price fell 6.7% from June to September 2026 to $71.85/kWh [source.benchmarkminerals.com](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/lithium-cost-pass-through-drives-volatile-quarter-for-energy-storage-cells-cell-price-review-q3-2026).
    *   Despite falling pack prices ($108/kWh in 2025) and declining cell costs, per-kWh pack costs are expected to stay relatively stable or rise slightly, with projected ranges of roughly $75–$90/kWh [mckinsey.com.br](https://www.mckinsey.com.br/features/mckinsey-center-for-future-mobility/our-insights/battery-2035-building-new-advantages).

### Environmental Impact and Circularity

*   **Manufacturing Emissions and Resource Use**
    *   LFP batteries have a significantly lower global warming potential during the manufacturing phase (approx. 573 kg CO2-eq) compared to NMC (approx. 1208 kg CO2-eq) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esd.2025.101837).
    *   NMC batteries use approximately six times more water in manufacturing (153.6 m3) than LFP batteries (25.8 m3) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esd.2025.101837).
    *   LFP has the lowest environmental impacts per kg during raw material extraction and processing due to lower emissions [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.7302/27571).
    *   Raw material extraction for NMC is higher than for LFP but can be mitigated by end-of-life material recovery [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833).

*   **Use Phase Emissions**
    *   NMC batteries have higher use-phase emissions (approx. 1042 kg CO2-eq) compared to LFP (approx. 706 kg CO2-eq) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esd.2025.101837).
    *   The use phase electricity consumption dominates the global warming potential across scenarios, accounting for approximately 75% [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833).

*   **End-of-Life and Recycling**
    *   Recycling provides limited mitigation of emissions, contributing less than 2% of total emissions in some scenarios [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esd.2025.101837).
    *   NMC batteries generally show greater environmental impact reductions from recycling than LFP [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.7302/27571).
    *   For LFP batteries, reuse before recycling yields higher long-term profits and lower emissions [nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52030-0).
    *   For NMC batteries, direct recycling becomes most profitable as SOH rises [nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52030-0).
    *   NMC batteries are 6–25% more circular than LFP, even though LFP has a 33% longer lifetime, due to higher material recovery ratios (13–24% higher for NMC) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833).
    *   Hydrometallurgical recycling (HyR) is more economical for LFP, while direct recycling is more economical for NMC [nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52030-0).
    *   NMC with hydrometallurgy recycling (HyR) yields the best overall environmental and circular performance [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833).

### Applications and Design Considerations

*   **EV Applications**
    *   NMC may be preferable for long-range cars due to higher energy delivery and range [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182).
    *   LFP offers a longer cycle life and lower heat risk, making it suitable for buses, delivery vehicles, and stationary storage [intechopen.com](https://www.intechopen.com/online-first/1257182).
    *   LFP supports prismatic and blade formats well, aiding secure, cost-efficient integration in EVs and storage [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   NMC and NCA are favored in cylindrical and pouch formats for high-energy applications [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   The choice of chemistry should align with vehicle design, grid conditions, and recycling policy [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.7302/27571).

*   **Cell Form Factors and Architectures**
    *   Cell form factors (cylindrical, prismatic, pouch) and electrode architectures (jelly-roll, stacked, blade) affect performance, safety, and manufacturability across battery chemistries [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   Cylindrical cells offer mechanical robustness but lower volumetric energy density due to packing efficiency [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   Prismatic and blade designs enable tighter packaging and higher energy density per volume, especially for LFP [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   Pouch cells provide high energy-to-weight and flexible packaging but require precise mechanical compression [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).
    *   Jelly-roll and multi-tab/tabless configurations improve uniform current distribution and enable higher energy/power in NMC/NCA chemistries [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries11120450).

This report compares Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) and Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) lithium-ion batteries, focusing on their characteristics and implications for electric vehicles (EVs).

### Performance and Durability

*   **Thermal Resilience and Degradation**
    *   LFP batteries offer superior thermal resilience and a longer cycle life under hot conditions [S1].
    *   NMC batteries degrade more rapidly than LFP batteries above 50°C and are more vulnerable to thermal stress [S1].
    *   At 60°C, LFP batteries retain approximately 80% State of Health (SOH) for roughly twice as many cycles as NMC batteries [S1].
    *   LFP batteries also show lower resistance growth and steadier coulombic efficiency across various temperatures compared to NMC [S1].
    *   NMC cells generate more heat during fast charging, while LFP cells run cooler with more consistent and lower surface temperatures [S3].

*   **Power and Energy Delivery**
    *   NMC cells generally deliver higher power output and are preferable for long-range cars due to higher energy delivery and range [S3][S4].
    *   LFP batteries typically have lower voltage and energy density compared to NMC [S4].
    *   The use phase of NMC batteries generally outperforms LFP in energy efficiency due to lower battery mass [S14].

*   **Fast Charging**
    *   LFP cells can charge to 100% SOH in less than half the time of other chemistries, offering a unique advantage in fast charging duration [S2].
    *   Despite variations in energy density, fast charging and heat generation characteristics are relatively similar across LFP, NMC, and NCA cells, suggesting convergence in design goals among manufacturers to manage heat effectively [S2].
    *   Thermal management is critical for maintaining fast charging performance, regardless of chemistry [S2][S3].

*   **Cycle Life**
    *   LFP batteries offer a longer cycle life [S3][S4][S9].
    *   NMC batteries generally have a shorter cycle life compared to LFP [S8].

### Cost and Market Dynamics

*   **Cost of Materials and Cells**
    *   LFP chemistry replaces expensive nickel and cobalt, making LFP batteries generally cheaper than nickel-based cells [S7].
    *   The cathode active material (CAM) accounts for 40-50% of a nickel-based cell's cost and 25-30% of an LFP cell's cost, making it the most expensive and difficult-to-secure component [S5].
    *   In Q3 2026, LFP 314Ah prices fluctuated, rising in July and falling in August, but Europe and North America prices remained above China [S6].
    *   LFP pack prices can be discounted by roughly 36.7% to over 40% compared to NMC [S12].
    *   Lithium-ion battery prices have dropped over 90% from 2010–2024 [S9].

*   **Market Share and Production**
    *   LFP accounts for over 55% of deployed EV batteries worldwide [S12].
    *   Outside China, about 80% of deployed EV batteries use nickel-containing chemistries (NMC) [S12].
    *   China produces over 75% of global lithium-ion cells, with most supply chain components concentrated domestically, contributing to lower prices [S7][S10].
    *   The current EV battery mix is roughly 50/50 between LFP and NMC, with LFP being the fastest-growing due to lower cost and longer cycle life [S9].
    *   Chinese producers supply about 75% of global EV battery deployment [S12].

*   **Overcapacity and Pricing Trends**
    *   Overcapacity in the battery market (about 900 GWh in 2025) persists, mainly driven by Asian manufacturers [S10].
    *   Q3 2026 saw broad price declines across most battery cell grades [S6].
    *   The global Lithium Ion Battery price fell 6.7% from June to September 2026 to $71.85/kWh [S6].
    *   Despite falling pack prices ($108/kWh in 2025) and declining cell costs, per-kWh pack costs are expected to stay relatively stable or rise slightly, with projected ranges of roughly $75–$90/kWh [S10].

### Environmental Impact and Circularity

*   **Manufacturing Emissions and Resource Use**
    *   LFP batteries have a significantly lower global warming potential during the manufacturing phase (approx. 573 kg CO2-eq) compared to NMC (approx. 1208 kg CO2-eq) [S13].
    *   NMC batteries use approximately six times more water in manufacturing (153.6 m3) than LFP batteries (25.8 m3) [S13].
    *   LFP has the lowest environmental impacts per kg during raw material extraction and processing due to lower emissions [S14].
    *   Raw material extraction for NMC is higher than for LFP but can be mitigated by end-of-life material recovery [S16].

*   **Use Phase Emissions**
    *   NMC batteries have higher use-phase emissions (approx. 1042 kg CO2-eq) compared to LFP (approx. 706 kg CO2-eq) [S13].
    *   The use phase electricity consumption dominates the global warming potential across scenarios, accounting for approximately 75% [S16].

*   **End-of-Life and Recycling**
    *   Recycling provides limited mitigation of emissions, contributing less than 2% of total emissions in some scenarios [S13].
    *   NMC batteries generally show greater environmental impact reductions from recycling than LFP [S14].
    *   For LFP batteries, reuse before recycling yields higher long-term profits and lower emissions [S15].
    *   For NMC batteries, direct recycling becomes most profitable as SOH rises [S15].
    *   NMC batteries are 6–25% more circular than LFP, even though LFP has a 33% longer lifetime, due to higher material recovery ratios (13–24% higher for NMC) [S16].
    *   Hydrometallurgical recycling (HyR) is more economical for LFP, while direct recycling is more economical for NMC [S15].
    *   NMC with hydrometallurgy recycling (HyR) yields the best overall environmental and circular performance [S16].

### Applications and Design Considerations

*   **EV Applications**
    *   NMC may be preferable for long-range cars due to higher energy delivery and range [S3].
    *   LFP offers a longer cycle life and lower heat risk, making it suitable for buses, delivery vehicles, and stationary storage [S3].
    *   LFP supports prismatic and blade formats well, aiding secure, cost-efficient integration in EVs and storage [S4].
    *   NMC and NCA are favored in cylindrical and pouch formats for high-energy applications [S4].
    *   The choice of chemistry should align with vehicle design, grid conditions, and recycling policy [S14].

*   **Cell Form Factors and Architectures**
    *   Cell form factors (cylindrical, prismatic, pouch) and electrode architectures (jelly-roll, stacked, blade) affect performance, safety, and manufacturability across battery chemistries [S4].
    *   Cylindrical cells offer mechanical robustness but lower volumetric energy density due to packing efficiency [S4].
    *   Prismatic and blade designs enable tighter packaging and higher energy density per volume, especially for LFP [S4].
    *   Pouch cells provide high energy-to-weight and flexible packaging but require precise mechanical compression [S4].
    *   Jelly-roll and multi-tab/tabless configurations improve uniform current distribution and enable higher energy/power in NMC/NCA chemistries [S4].

  - Overall: LFP outperformed NMC across air pollution, water pollution, and toxicity indicators; more suitable for India’s cost-sensitive, resource-constrained context.
- Implications: Supports prioritizing LFP batteries for India’s low-carbon EV ecosystem, while highlighting the need to strengthen end-of-life recycling infrastructure.
- Scope note: Findings specific to Indian conditions and current recycling constraints; results may differ with changes in electricity mix and recycling technology.

Essential results:

- Study compares SOH diagnosis and forecasting for LFP vs. NMC lithium-ion batteries in EVs under realistic cycling and temperatures from 25°C to 65°C.
- Key finding: Both chemistries degrade faster as temperature rises, but NMC ages much more rapidly above 50°C.
- At elevated temperatures (e.g., 60–65°C), LFP maintains superior performance:
  - Slower capacity fade (SOH decline)
  - Lower internal resistance growth
  - Higher coulombic efficiency
  - Retains 80% SOH for roughly twice as many cycles as NMC at 60°C
- NMC shows significantly accelerated aging beyond 50°C, with greater variability in degradation and higher failure risk under thermal stress.
- Quantitative insight: LFP consistently outperforms NMC across all temperatures in cycle life, resistance, and efficiency; the performance gap widens with temperature.
- Practical implications: Chemistry selection and thermal management are crucial for EVs in hot climates or high-duty applications; results support targeted battery management strategies and adaptive thermal design.
- Methodology: A validated multi-temperature, simulation-based benchmark tracking capacity fade, resistance growth, and coulombic efficiency as SOH indicators.

results.search_result:
EV battery chemistries vary to balance cost, range, and performance. Key takeaways:

- No single best chemistry; automakers choose based on trade-offs in cost, energy density, thermal stability, and cycle life.
- LMO (manganese-based cathode): cheaper, thermally stable, high power, fast charging, but faster degradation and lower energy density; used in early EVs but largely out of favor for long-range.
- NMC (nickel–manganese–cobalt): energy-dense with an established supply/manufacture base; common in longer-range EVs from many automakers (e.g., Hyundai, Kia, BMW, VW, Toyota). Drawbacks include higher cost, reduced cold-temperature range, and lower thermal stability.
- LFP (iron phosphate): cheaper, safer, long cycle life; energy density is lower. Popular in China and growing in the U.S./Europe for affordable models; often improved with design tweaks (prismatic cells, cell-to-pack).
- LMFP/LMR: manganese-enhanced variants aimed at reducing nickel/cobalt reliance and cost, while maintaining range similar to NMC.
- Solid-state vs. conventional lithium-ion: solid-state uses solid electrolytes (ceramic/polymer/sulfide) and promises higher range, faster charging, and better durability, but mass production cost and defect challenges slow adoption. Semi-solid (gel-like) variants are expected to reach market first.
- Cell formats and packaging (cylindrical, pouch, prismatic) and how cells are integrated (modules vs. direct pack/chassis) significantly influence real-world EV performance, beyond the chemistry alone.

Bottom line: EV battery choice is a multi-factor optimization (cost, range, charge speed, temperature performance, longevity, and supply chain). Solid-state and semi-solid goals are to improve performance and safety, but manufacturing maturity will shape adoption timelines.

Summary:
- The paper compares major EV battery chemistries: lead-acid, NiMH, Li-ion variants (NMC and LFP), plus emerging solid-state and sodium-ion batteries.
- Key evaluation metrics: energy density, power, cycle life, charging characteristics, safety, thermal behavior, cost, and material sustainability.
- Findings:
  - Lead-acid and NiMH are largely unsuitable for modern EVs due to low energy density (lead-acid) and moderate-to-high self-discharge (NiMH).
  - Li-ion NMC provides high energy density and power but faces thermal safety, cobalt dependency, and cost volatility concerns.
  - Li-ion LFP offers superior thermal stability, safety, longer cycle life, and lower cost, making it attractive for mass-market and commercial EVs, albeit with lower energy density and potentially reduced driving range.
  - Solid-state batteries promise ultra-high energy density and enhanced safety but face manufacturing, scaling, and cost barriers.
  - Sodium-ion batteries offer a cheap, sustainable alternative with abundant materials and good safety, but currently deliver lower energy density, limiting them to short-range or entry-level EVs.
- Short-term outlook: NMC and LFP will dominate, with LFP gaining traction in price-sensitive and commercial segments.
- Long-term outlook: solid-state and sodium-ion may shape future EV architectures, contingent on overcoming cost, scaling, and manufacturing challenges.
- Additional considerations: end-of-life management, thermal runaway risks, and reliance on cobalt/nickel highlight sustainability and ethical sourcing concerns; battery management systems and strategies to extend lifespan are emphasized.
- Overall conclusion: No single chemistry satisfies all requirements; optimal battery selection depends on vehicle type and application. Emerging chemistries offer potential to address gaps (safety, sustainability, cost) while solid-state and sodium-ion are poised to influence the long-term evolution of EV batteries.

results.search_result:
Summary:
- NMC batteries: Higher energy density (150–250 Wh/kg) but higher cost and safety risks (cobalt and nickel materials; risk of thermal runaway). Favored for premium, long-range EVs.
- LFP batteries: Lower energy density (90–160 Wh/kg) but cheaper, safer (stable up to ~400°C), and longer-lasting (2,000–5,000 cycles). Made from iron and phosphate (no Ni/Co); lower environmental and ethical concerns; easier recycling.
- Why switch to LFP:
  1) Cost reduction: ~$80–$100/kWh vs $100–$130/kWh for NMC.
  2) Safety: Greater thermal stability.
  3) Supply security: Avoids cobalt and nickel markets.
  4) Sustainability: Simpler, greener materials and recycling.
  5) Market fit: Ideal for budget EVs and stationary storage; strong growth in LFP share (about 40% of EV battery market globally in 2024; ~60% in China).
  6) Cycle life advantage: 2,000–5,000 cycles (sometimes up to ~6,000 in advanced designs) vs 1,000–2,000 for NMC.
- Cathode/chemistry: LFP = LiFePO4, stable olivine structure, no Ni/Co; requires enhancements (e.g., carbon coatings) to boost conductivity.
- Trade-offs: Lower voltage per cell (~3.2 V) and lower energy density necessitate larger/heavier packs; processing costs for conductivity improvements.

Bottom line: NMC offers high energy density for premium long-range EVs at higher cost and safety risk, while LFP provides cheaper, safer, longer-lasting chemistry better suited for budget EVs, grid storage, and markets prioritizing cost and durability.

  - Circularity: NMC is 6-25% more circular than LFP. This advantage persists despite LFP’s longer lifetime (LFP ~33% longer).
  - Material recovery: NMC shows higher material recovery ratios, contributing to better circularity.
  - Environmental performance: NMC delivers 3-6% lower GWP and 12-16% lower ADPm per kWh delivered than LFP (e.g., GWP 22.9–37.7 g CO2 eq./kWh; ADPm 1.3–1.6 mg Sb eq./kWh).
- Best configuration: NMC with HyR recycling (Hydrometallurgy with Recycling) provides the highest circularity and lowest environmental burden (0.56 kg CO2 eq. and 8.6 mg Sb eq. per kWh delivered).
- Exception: LFP with HyR-BLE (very long lifetime scenario ~400,000 km) achieves the best PCI and environmental savings in that sensitivity case.
- Important caveats: Circularity indicators (CI and PCI) largely reflect the recycling stage; they do not capture all life cycle aspects (e.g., electricity mix during use, active component impacts). A full life cycle assessment (LCA) is needed to validate and complement circularity results. A holistic approach linking circularity with life cycle thinking is recommended for EV batteries.

- Goal: Assess strategies to reach circular supply chains for lithium, cobalt, and nickel in Europe for EVs, weighing material demand, mining, and recycling needs.
- Key finding: Achieving circularity requires substantial upfront mining- and recycling-capacity shifts, but optimizing strategies can markedly reduce primary material demand and emissions.

  - The “optimal overall” scenario accelerates circularity for Li, Co, Ni by ~45, 18, and 22 years respectively versus baseline.

1) Resource sufficiency — risks of relying on finite materials as demand grows.
2) Geographical distribution and global value chains — uneven material availability and geopolitical implications.
3) Regulation and policies — how governance shapes supply security and environmental/social outcomes.
4) Circular economy — potential for material reuse/recycling to reduce virgin material demand and environmental impact.
5) Emerging battery technologies — how new chemistries and designs may alter material needs and supply chains.

The authors emphasize the complex, interdependent causalities across technology, environment, society, economy, and politics (the “wicked” nature of the problem). They extend existing techno-industrial analyses by incorporating political dimensions, governance of land use and electricity, and the role of industrial policy. The study concludes that pathways forward must account these interdependencies and promote integrated strategies across policy, innovation, and circular economy approaches to improve sustainability in EV battery materials.

## LFP vs. NMC Lithium-Ion Batteries for Electric Vehicles

### Overview and Market Trends

*   **No Single Best Chemistry:** Automakers select battery chemistries based on trade-offs in cost, energy density, thermal stability, and cycle life [insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/782685/all-ev-battery-chemistries-explained/). There is no single battery chemistry that fulfills all requirements for electric vehicles (EVs); optimal selection depends on the vehicle type and application [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139).
*   **Dominance of LFP and NMC:** Lithium-ion (Li-ion) variants, specifically Nickel-Manganese-Cobalt (NMC) and Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP), will dominate the short-term outlook for EV batteries, with LFP gaining traction in price-sensitive and commercial segments [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139).
*   **LFP Market Share Growth:** LFP batteries are increasingly dominant globally. In January–August, LFP accounted for 65.4% of total global EV cathode shipments, up 5.0 points year-over-year [biz.heraldcorp.com](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10899351). This includes a 34.9% share in non-China markets, an increase of 14.1 points [biz.heraldcorp.com](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10899351). In China, LFP's market share in traction battery installations reached 85.5% in September 2026, with ternary (NMC/other) batteries declining [latestevnews.com](https://www.latestevnews.com/articles/chinas-battery-market-lfp-reaches-855percent). For the first nine months of 2026, LFP held an 82.8% share of traction batteries installed in China [latestevnews.com](https://www.latestevnews.com/articles/chinas-battery-market-lfp-reaches-855percent). The China electric car market report for 2025 indicates LFP held approximately 57.24% share of battery chemistry [mordorintelligence.com](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/china-electric-car-market).
*   **OEM Strategy Shift:** EV manufacturers are re-evaluating investments and shifting strategies towards cheaper chemistries like LFP, driven by lower-than-expected production volumes and financial losses [automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com](https://www.automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com/electrification/ev-batteries-oems-cut-investment-due-to-lower-demand/2625022). US automakers are deepening collaboration with China for LFP battery technology while pursuing decoupling in vehicle production, relying on cost-competitive Chinese batteries [en.sedaily.com](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/02/05/us-automakers-deepen-china-battery-ties-while-pushing). SK On, a Korean supplier, signed a significant LFP supply deal with Posco Future M for energy storage systems (ESS) and U.S. plant deliveries [biz.heraldcorp.com](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10899351).

### Performance Characteristics

*   **Energy Density:** NMC batteries offer higher energy density, typically ranging from 150–250 Wh/kg, making them suitable for premium, long-range EVs [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). LFP batteries have lower energy density, usually between 90–160 Wh/kg [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). This lower energy density often necessitates larger and heavier battery packs for LFP to achieve comparable range [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries).
*   **Cycle Life:** LFP batteries generally offer a longer cycle life, ranging from 2,000 to 5,000 cycles, and sometimes up to 6,000 cycles in advanced designs [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). NMC batteries typically have a cycle life of 1,000 to 2,000 cycles [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries).
*   **Thermal Stability and Safety:** LFP batteries demonstrate superior thermal stability and safety, remaining stable up to approximately 400°C and having a lower risk of thermal runaway [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139) [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). NMC batteries have lower thermal stability and a higher safety risk [insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/782685/all-ev-battery-chemistries-explained/) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139).
*   **Temperature Performance:** Both LFP and NMC batteries degrade faster as temperature rises, but NMC ages much more rapidly above 50°C [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489). At elevated temperatures (e.g., 60–65°C), LFP maintains superior performance, showing slower capacity fade (SOH decline), lower internal resistance growth, and higher coulombic efficiency [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489). At 60°C, LFP retains 80% State of Health (SOH) for roughly twice as many cycles as NMC [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.53375/ijecer.2025.489).
*   **Cold Temperature Performance:** NMC batteries may experience reduced range in cold temperatures [insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/782685/all-ev-battery-chemistries-explained/).

### Economic and Supply Chain Considerations

*   **Cost:** LFP batteries are generally cheaper than NMC, with pack costs around €64/kWh for LFP compared to €82/kWh for NMC [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries) [mckinsey.com](https://www.mckinsey.com/features/mckinsey-center-for-future-mobility/our-insights/the-future-of-affordable-evs-breakthroughs-in-battery-pack-costs). LFP is made from abundant iron and phosphate, avoiding reliance on more expensive and volatile materials like nickel and cobalt [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). This results in LFP costing approximately $80–$100/kWh, while NMC costs $100–$130/kWh [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries).
*   **Material Sourcing and Sustainability:** LFP batteries do not use nickel or cobalt, reducing environmental and ethical concerns associated with their mining and providing better supply security [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries). NMC batteries have higher costs and material dependency on cobalt and nickel, which face sustainability and ethical sourcing concerns [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139).
*   **Recycling and Circularity:** NMC batteries are generally more circular and have lower environmental burdens than LFP, showing 6–25% higher circularity and achieving higher material recovery ratios [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833). NMC with hydrometallurgical recycling provides the highest circularity and lowest environmental burden [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2024.107833). For LFP batteries, profit and emissions are maximized when reuse occurs before recycling [nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52030-0). Adopting LFP batteries is a core strategy to improve circularity for lithium, cobalt, and nickel in EV supply chains, reducing primary material demand [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resourpol.2024.105160).
*   **Geographical Concentration:** China dominates the supply chain for upstream materials, particularly those used in LFP, leading to lower delivered costs in China compared to North America and Europe, which face higher material costs due to limited midstream capacity [mckinsey.com](https://www.mckinsey.com/mgi/our-research/batteries-scaling-the-engine-of-electrification).

### Application and Outlook

*   **LFP Applications:** LFP batteries are popular in China and are gaining traction in the U.S. and Europe for affordable EV models [insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/782685/all-ev-battery-chemistries-explained/). They are ideal for budget EVs, mass-market EVs, commercial vehicles, and stationary storage due to their lower cost, enhanced safety, and longer cycle life [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139) [electronics360.globalspec.com](https://electronics360.globalspec.com/article/22873/from-nmc-to-lfp-batteries).
*   **NMC Applications:** NMC batteries are common in longer-range EVs from many automakers, including Hyundai, Kia, BMW, VW, and Toyota, due to their higher energy density [insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/782685/all-ev-battery-chemistries-explained/).
*   **Future Outlook:** While NMC and LFP will dominate in the short term, emerging chemistries like solid-state and sodium-ion batteries are expected to influence the long-term evolution of EV batteries by offering potential improvements in safety, sustainability, and cost, provided manufacturing and scaling challenges are overcome [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.47392/irjaeh.2026.0139).

Summary:
- NMC batteries: Higher energy density (150–250 Wh/kg) but higher cost and safety risks (cobalt and nickel materials; risk of thermal runaway). Favored for premium, long-range EVs.
- LFP batteries: Lower energy density (90–160 Wh/kg) but cheaper, safer (stable up to ~400°C), and longer-lasting (2,000–5,000 cycles). Made from iron and phosphate (no Ni/Co); lower environmental and ethical concerns; easier recycling.
- Why switch to LFP:
  1) Cost reduction: ~$80–$100/kWh vs $100–$130/kWh for NMC.
  2) Safety: Greater thermal stability.
  3) Supply security: Avoids cobalt and nickel markets.
  4) Sustainability: Simpler, greener materials and recycling.
  5) Market fit: Ideal for budget EVs and stationary storage; strong growth in LFP share (about 40% of EV battery market globally in 2024; ~60% in China).
  6) Cycle life advantage: 2,000–5,000 cycles (sometimes up to ~6,000 in advanced designs) vs 1,000–2,000 for NMC.
- Cathode/chemistry: LFP = LiFePO4, stable olivine structure, no Ni/Co; requires enhancements (e.g., carbon coatings) to boost conductivity.
- Trade-offs: Lower voltage per cell (~3.2 V) and lower energy density necessitate larger/heavier packs; processing costs for conductivity improvements.

Bottom line: NMC offers high energy density for premium long-range EVs at higher cost and safety risk, while LFP provides cheaper, safer, longer-lasting chemistry better suited for budget EVs, grid storage, and markets prioritizing cost and durability.

Summary:
- EV market underdelivered: production volumes lagged expectations, triggering a costly industry reset now estimated around $60 billion, with further future losses likely.
- OEMs cutting investment and dissolving battery JV momentum: several automakers are exiting battery supplier joint ventures or slashing planned battery investments, straining battery suppliers’ financial viability.
- Notable failures and restructurings:
  - Porsche closed its Cellforce battery unit (cost ≥€300m), impacting suppliers like Grob Werke.
  - Ford and SK On dissolved the Blue Oval SK JV (US$11.4b planned build-out of three factories) amid continuing losses in Ford’s Model e unit.
  - Ford’s Model e losses: ~$5.1b in 2024, ~$4.7b in 2023, and an additional ~$4.8b announced in 2025.
  - Honda bought out LG from the Ohio battery plant JV (US$2.8b) after a broader plan to reduce EV investment by over US$20b through 2030, with potential shift of the plant toward ESS (energy storage systems).
- Supply chain impact: billions in planned investments in battery production are being scaled back or reassessed; several suppliers may face financial stress in the medium term.
- Broader implications: shifts toward cheaper chemistries (LFP), diversification into non-vehicle battery uses (ESS, data-centre storage, robotics), and strategic realignment of partnerships as the EV growth scenario changes.

Summary:
- US automakers (Ford, GM, Stellantis) are pursuing a dual strategy: deepen China battery technology collaboration (using China’s CATL LFP batteries) while actively pursuing decoupling from China in vehicle production.
- They are expanding US and European manufacturing but rely on cost-competitive Chinese batteries due to economic pressures and EV subsidy/tariff policies under the Trump administration.
- In response to reshoring policies and potential tariff wars, GM is moving China-produced models to the US; Ford is diversifying supply chains to Thailand, Vietnam, and Canada.
- The shift negatively impacts Korea’s battery industry, with Ford and SK On and LG Energy Solution contract terminations signaling a need for Korea to develop domestic alternatives.
- Overall, the report highlights a paradox: decoupling rhetoric coexists with increasing dependence on Chinese battery technology.

Global EV cathode shipments rose 21.8% in Jan–Aug year-over-year to 1.917 million tons, driven by a surge in LFP (lithium iron phosphate) materials. LFP now accounts for 65.4% of total shipments (up 5.0 points) and 34.9% of non-China markets (up 14.1 points). LFP shipments grew 31.8% to 1.254 million tons, while ternary materials (NCM and others) grew only 6.4% to 663,000 tons.

Key regional trends:
- Outside China: shipments up 30.0% to 733,000 tons, strengthening LFP’s share in Europe, Asia, and other overseas markets.
- LFP is expanding beyond China to become dominant in multiple regions; the gap between LFP and ternaries widened to 25.4 percentage points.

Top suppliers (by cathode chemistry):
- LFP: Rofar (3rd overall among LFP), Yuneng (leader), Wanlun, Gotion, Shenghua Tech among fast growers.
- Ternaries: Ronbay led with 90,900 tons; Reshine 73,800 tons; Libode and L&F posting notable gains; Ecopro shipments declined.

Corporate and regional composition:
- Chinese suppliers: 87.3% of the market (up 3.3 points).
- Korean and Japanese suppliers declined to 9.0% and 3.6%, respectively.

Notable developments:
- SK On signed a ~1.1 trillion won LFP supply deal with Posco Future M for ESS and U.S. Georgia plant deliveries (2027–2029).
- Market focus shifting toward LFP due to higher energy density needs and regulatory pressures (North American EU content rules, battery passport by 2027).

Bottom line: LFP is increasingly dominant in global EV cathodes, widening its lead over ternaries, with Europe and other regions accelerating adoption and supply-chain shifts driven by policy and regional content requirements.

- The two most common cathode chemistries are NMC (nickel–manganese–cobalt) and LFP (lithium iron phosphate).

Global battery production has scaled rapidly, with expected lithium-ion phosphate (LFP) demand reaching about 1.6 TWh in 2025. - Regional dynamics: Battery production is highly concentrated in Asia (over 75% of advanced batteries). Proximity to input suppliers lowers costs for regions closer to input production.
- Upstream/Midstream value chain: The value chain spans mining and refining of materials (Li, Ni, Co, Mn, Fe, P, Al, Cu, graphite), processing into battery-grade inputs, production of active materials for cathodes/anodes, electrolytes and separators, and final cell assembly. Scale and supplier depth at each stage reduce costs and lead times.
- Cost drivers and regional gaps: Materials are the largest cost driver (about 40% of regional cost differences). Regions like Europe and the US face higher material costs per kWh (roughly $7 more) than China, with Malaysia around $3 extra. Limited midstream capacity (e.g., LFP cathode, graphite anode) in non-Chinese regions amplifies costs due to freight, tariffs, compliance, and margins. Until U.S. and European midstream capacity scales, imported materials or long-haul sourcing will keep costs higher.
- Future demand outlook: Announced capacity broadly covers global demand through 2030, but regional imbalances persist.
